![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/39431059174ad545642732d57f40689e13af962ed2bc091b86eb0d4f41717299.png)

The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ are given above. Find ${h}^{′}(2)$ where $h(x)=-2f(x)+3g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
The addition and constant multiple rules for derivatives give

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=-2{f}^{′}(x)+3{g}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(2)=-2{f}^{′}(2)+3{g}^{′}(2).
$$

Also, notice that $x=2$ corresponds to 

- the interval $x\in (1,3)$ for the function $f,$ and

- the interval $x\in (1,3)$ for the function $g,$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252554/assets/33082034fa45d3228168431e8263c5a9f2c557ce26a8d637596a1e4e6d47d314.png)

- The slope of $y=f(x)$ is constant on $x\in (1,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{2-1}{3-1}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(2)=\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of $y=g(x)$ is constant on $x\in (1,3)$ and equals

$$
\frac{Δg}{Δx}=\frac{3-(-1)}{3-1}=2.
$$

Therefore, ${g}^{′}(2)=2.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =-2{f}^{′}(2)+3{g}^{′}(2) \\  & =(-2)\cdot \frac{1}{2}+3\cdot 2 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
